question: Should OpenClaw permanently add localized command descriptions to the shared Gateway command and plugin-facing metadata contract, or keep localization owned by individual presentation surfaces until a narrower contract is designed?
rationale: This is an additive public-facing protocol and plugin metadata direction with cross-client compatibility consequences; it cannot be resolved safely by a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Approve a narrow shared contract
options.body: Sponsor `descriptionLocalizations` with documented ownership, legacy-client behavior, supported locale semantics, and compatibility tests before landing dependent surfaces.

options.title: Keep localization at presentation boundaries
options.body: Remove the new Gateway command field and let Control UI and channel owners localize their own built-in presentation until a separately approved protocol design exists.

options.title: Pause the cumulative series
options.body: Hold the branch until the RFC or designated owners establish the product and plugin-contract direction.

recommendation.title: Keep localization at presentation boundaries
recommendation.body: Remove the new Gateway command field and let Control UI and channel owners localize their own built-in presentation until a separately approved protocol design exists.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable current-main ownership trail was available in the supplied review data; the decision should be made by the Gateway/plugin API owners rather than inferred from the contributor branch.
